info.title: torrentd
info.summary: Control plane of a headless, multi-account torrent seeding daemon.
info.description: The `/v1` HTTP API of `torrentd`. Conventions — authentication, pagination, errors, and what may change within v1 — are in `docs/api/README.md`; every problem `type` URI resolves to a heading in `docs/api/problems.md`.

get.description:
`profiles` is the **live** count — sessions that came up — and
`profiles_failed` is how many configured profiles never got one. They are
reported separately because a payload that only ever showed the live count
gave no hint an account was missing.

A daemon running **no** live session answers 503 whatever the reason — it
is the state a total bring-up failure produces. Some-but-not-all failed
stays 200: the profiles that did come up are serving, and taking the
daemon out of rotation would stop them too. `profiles_failed` and
`torrentd_profile_vpn_tunnel_up` are what to alert on for that. The route is
unauthenticated: a probe that needs a credential is a probe that breaks
during the incident it exists to detect.

X-Request-Id.description: The identifier this request is correlated by

Cache-Control.description:
`no-store`: every response describes live daemon state, and most of
it is only readable with a credential.

503.description: The daemon is unready; `reason` says why. Take it out of rotation.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events. Each message's `data` is a JSON `ServerEvent`; today
that is only `tick`, sent when anything a client renders may have changed
and at least every ten seconds. A comment line keeps the connection alive
every fifteen seconds through proxies that drop idle ones. The stream ends
when the daemon shuts down; reconnect after the `retry` the first event
carries.

post.description:
The same as `SIGHUP`. The file stays the single source of truth: a client
can ask the daemon to re-read it, not tell the daemon what it says.
Several keys are reloadable (`log_level`, `upload_rate_limit`,
`connections_limit`, `aio_threads`, `enable_lsd`,
`max_concurrent_http_announces`); the reload task logs what it applied and
warns about anything that needs a restart. `202` means the request was
queued, not that it succeeded.

get.description:
Every torrent the daemon holds an assignment for, loaded or not, ordered
by infohash and paged with `cursor`. Filter by `profile_id` and `phase`.
Rates, totals and phase come from the state the alert loop keeps, so a
page costs no call into libtorrent. Each item is a `TorrentSummary`; what
only a session can answer — name, size, save path, upload limit — is on
`GET /v1/torrents/{infohash}`.

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description:
Only the torrents assigned to this profile. A profile that failed to
come up is still listed; an id no profile declares is
`404 profile-not-found`, not an empty page.

parameters.description: Only the torrents in this phase.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Resume after the page this cursor ended.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Torrents per page, 1 to 1000; 100 when absent.

post.description:
From a magnet URI, a `.torrent` on the daemon's filesystem, or a
`.torrent` in the request (base64). The infohash is computed before any
session sees the torrent, so an infohash already assigned anywhere is
`409 torrent-exists` and the session never receives a duplicate. A
`.torrent` must announce to one of the profile's `allowed_tracker_domains`
when it sets any. The response is the torrent as its session first reports
it; its `phase` is `unknown` until the first state update.

delete.description:
Removes it from its session and clears its assignment, so the infohash can
be added again. `delete_files=true` also deletes the payload, and needs
`[pool] allow_mutations`. A torrent whose profile has no running session,
or that the boot left unloaded, is cleared from the daemon's records
alone (`delete_files` is refused there: nothing can reach the payload). A
torrent still being added is `409 torrent-adding`; retry once it lists a
phase other than `unknown`.

post.description:
Re-hashes the payload against the piece hashes. `202`: libtorrent checks
asynchronously, and the torrent's `phase` reports `checking` until it is
done. Needs no `[pool]`. A recheck drops seed mode, which is safe because
the no-download invariant rests on upload mode, and that survives it.
Refused while the profile is fenced, as resuming is.

post.summary: Pause every torrent in one profile.
post.description:
A fenced (`vpn_down`) profile is paused too: its torrents are already
paused, and pausing again is harmless. A profile that never came up has
nothing loaded to pause and answers `409 profile-unavailable` with its
bring-up failure. `failed_count` counts torrents the engine refused.

post.description:
Refused with `409 profile-unavailable` for a profile that never came up
(nothing of it is loaded) and for a fenced (`vpn_down`) one: its torrents
were paused because the tunnel is gone, and they stay paused until the
operator restarts the daemon. `failed_count` counts torrents the engine
refused.

post.description:
Every live profile is reached, fenced ones included: their torrents are
already paused, and pausing again is harmless. Profiles that never came up
are listed in `skipped_profiles`, since nothing of theirs is loaded. A
nonzero `failed_count` means some torrents are still running.

post.summary: Resume every torrent in every profile that is not fenced.
post.description:
A fenced (`vpn_down`) profile is skipped and listed in `skipped_profiles`,
not refused wholesale: one account's dead tunnel must not stop the others
resuming, and resuming it is exactly what the profile's own resume-all
refuses. Profiles that never came up are listed too.

post.description:
Works out every step the change would take and stores them as a `draft`,
touching nothing on disk; `POST …/apply` performs it. The planner refuses
with `409 plan-refused` when the change is unsafe as the index stands — an
overlap, drift, an occupied destination, a torrent not in the index.

Refused with `403 mutations-disabled` unless `[pool] allow_mutations` is
set. Creating a plan touches nothing, but a plan that can never be applied
is a trap, and refusing where the operator asks is the clearer signal.

post.description:
Hands library torrents whose payload the pool matched to one profile's
session. Each is claimed in the daemon's assignment registry first, so a
torrent another profile already holds is refused rather than announced from
a second account. A torrent whose previous client left trustworthy resume
data seeds at once (`fast_path`); any other is hashed by libtorrent before
it seeds (`queued_for_verification`). Torrents that are not `matched` are
refused, each with the reason. `dry_run` reports all of this and changes
nothing.

Not gated on `[pool] allow_mutations`: adoption records an existing file's
ownership and moves nothing on disk.

Asks libtorrent to check each torrent's payload against its piece hashes
(v1 SHA-1, v2 SHA-256 merkle) — the daemon's only authoritative check.
`202` means the checks started; each torrent reports `checking` until it
finishes. A torrent not loaded in any session is skipped with the reason.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity; The request is invalid

202.description: the request was accepted, and the processing it asked for has not completed

X-Request-Id.description: The identifier this request is correlated by

Cache-Control.description:
`no-store`: every response describes live daemon state, and most of
it is only readable with a credential.

413.description: the request body exceeds the configured limit

post.description:
Performs every step not yet done, in order, and waits for the last: a
large delete or a cross-device move can run for minutes. Each step is
journalled before it is attempted, and applying stops at the first failure
— answering `200` with `status: failed` and the plan's steps saying which
and why. A `failed` plan can be applied again to retry.

A plan that deletes data applies only with its `confirm_token`: not a
security control, but a guard against applying the wrong plan id. Refused
with `403 mutations-disabled` unless `[pool] allow_mutations` is set.

ok.description: Whether the daemon is ready. `true` exactly when the status is 200.

reason.description: Why the daemon is unready; `null` when it is ready.

profiles_fenced.description: Live profiles whose VPN tunnel the monitor fenced.

profiles_failed.description: Configured profiles that never came up.

heartbeat_age_secs.description:
Seconds since the alert loop last stamped its heartbeat; `null` when
there is no live session to run one.

HealthReport.description: The daemon's readiness, and the counts behind it.

mode.description:
`password` when `[auth]` is configured; `disabled` when the daemon runs
with `allow_unauthenticated`, admitting every request.

session_ttl_secs.description:
Lifetime of a session token from `POST /v1/sessions`, in seconds.
`null` when authentication is disabled.

configured.description:
Whether `[pool]` is configured. Without it every `/v1/pool` operation
answers `404 pool-not-configured`.

allow_mutations.description:
Whether `[pool] allow_mutations` is set: mutation plans and
`DELETE /v1/torrents/{infohash}?delete_files=true` need it.

api_version.description: The API version this document describes. Always `"1"` under `/v1`.

ServerInfo.description:
What this daemon is and which optional surfaces it has.

Fetch it once after authenticating: it tells a client which parts of the
API mean anything here, so it can hide the pool rather than discover
`pool-not-configured` one request at a time.

torrents_total.description: Torrents the daemon holds an assignment for, loaded or not.

paused.description: Torrents paused, by an operator or by a VPN fence.

checking.description:
Torrents libtorrent is hashing — the reason a freshly adopted pool is
not seeding yet.

disk_error.description:
Torrents whose last word from libtorrent was a file error; the
disk-error retry is working on them.

errored.description: Torrents libtorrent set an error on.

upload_rate_total.description: Total upload rate, in bytes per second.

download_rate_total.description:
Total download rate, in bytes per second. A seeding daemon keeps this
near zero.

pending_resume_count.description: Resume-data saves requested and not yet written.

Status.description: Aggregate counts and rates across every profile.

fingerprint.description:
An opaque summary of daemon state, 16 hex digits. It changes when
anything visible does, and is re-sent at least every ten seconds.

oneOf.description: Something a client renders may have changed; refetch what is on screen.

ServerEvent.description:
One message on `GET /v1/events`.

Tagged by `kind`, which is also the SSE `event:` name. The stream tells a
client *when* to refetch, not what changed: pushing deltas would mean
serialising per-torrent state on every tick, at a hundred thousand
torrents the cost the state map exists to avoid. New kinds may be added
within v1; a client ignores kinds it does not know.

PrincipalKind.description: What kind of credential authenticated a request.

Scope.description:
What a credential is allowed to do.

Deliberately coarse. A finer model invites the mistake of handing a scrape
token something it did not need; three levels are enough to keep Prometheus
away from the mutation endpoints.

kind.description:
`session` for a token from `POST /v1/sessions`, `token` for a static
token from the config, `anonymous` when authentication is disabled.

name.description: The static token's configured name; `null` for any other kind.

expires_at.description: When a session token expires; `null` for any other kind.

TorrentPhase.description: What a torrent is doing, as of the last state update libtorrent posted.

InfoHashHex.description:
A torrent's v1 infohash as the API spells it: 40 hex digits.

Emitted lowercase; accepted in either case, in a path and in a body alike.
Anything else is refused where it is parsed — a `400` in a path, a `422`
in a body — before a handler sees it.

profile_id.description:
The profile the torrent is assigned to. An infohash belongs to exactly
one profile.

phase.description:
What the torrent is doing. `unknown` when no state update has arrived
for it — it is still being added, or no session holds it.

progress.description: Fraction of the payload present and verified, 0 to 1.

upload_rate.description: Upload rate, in bytes per second.

download_rate.description:
Download rate, in bytes per second. A seeding daemon keeps this near
zero.

total_uploaded.description: Bytes uploaded this session, including protocol overhead.

total_payload_uploaded.description: Payload bytes uploaded this session, the figure ratios are judged on.

is_finished.description: Whether every wanted piece is present.

TorrentSummary.description:
One torrent, as a listing reports it: what the daemon's own state map
knows, read without asking any session.

`GET /v1/torrents/{infohash}` returns the fuller [`Torrent`], which adds
what only the torrent's session can say.

items.description: This page's items, in the collection's order.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; `null` on the last one.

TorrentPage.description: One page of torrents, ordered by infohash.

name.description: The torrent's name. `null` while a magnet has no metadata.

total_size.description: Total payload size in bytes. `null` while a magnet has no metadata.

upload_limit_bytes_per_sec.description:
This torrent's own upload limit in bytes per second; `null` when it
has none (the profile's and the daemon's limits still apply).

added_at.description: When the torrent was first added; `null` when libtorrent does not know.

TorrentSession.description: What a torrent's session reports about it.

session.description:
What the torrent's session reports. `null` exactly when no session
holds the torrent: it is still being added, its profile never came up,
or the session could not be asked (the daemon logs why).

Torrent.description: One torrent: its summary, and what its session reports.

path.description:
Torrent-relative, `/`-separated; for a multi-file torrent it starts
with the torrent's directory name.

downloaded.description: Bytes of this file covered by complete, verified pieces.

priority.description: Download priority, 0 (skip) to 7 (top); 4 is the default.

items.description: This page's items, in the collection's order.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; `null` on the last one.

TorrentFilePage.description: One page of a torrent's files, in index order.

TrackerStatus.description:
Where a tracker stands.

Derived in this order: `error` when the last announce failed (an error
text is present, or announces have failed and none has ever succeeded);
otherwise `updating` while an announce is in flight; otherwise `working`
once the tracker has answered an announce; otherwise `not_contacted`.

tier.description: The tier; lower tiers are tried first.

host.description:
The tracker's host, with its port when the URL names one. Empty when
the URL could not be parsed.

url.description:
The announce URL, shown only as far as it is known to carry no
credential: unchanged when it is a scheme, a plain host and port, and
a conventional path (`/announce`, `/scrape`, …) with no query;
otherwise `scheme://host/[redacted:<hash>]`, or the bare marker when
it does not parse. The hash tells two trackers apart without showing
either. The raw URL is never returned.

message.description:
The last announce's error when it failed, else the tracker's last
status message; `null` when there is neither. URLs in it are redacted
as `url` is.

next_announce_at.description: When the next announce is due; `null` when none is scheduled.

seeds.description: Seeds, as the tracker last reported; `null` when unknown.

peers.description:
Peers that are not seeds, as the tracker last reported; `null` when
unknown.

items.description: The trackers, tier by tier, in the order they are tried.

ProfileStatus.description: Whether a profile has a session, and whether its tunnel is up.

PortForwardMode.description: How a profile's listen port is chosen.

profile_id.description: The profile's id, as its `[[profile]]` table names it.

status.description: Whether the profile has a session, and whether its tunnel is up.

tunnel_ip.description:
The tunnel's address; `null` for a host profile, a failed one, or
before the tunnel reported one.

torrent_count.description:
Torrents assigned to this profile, loaded or not. For a `failed`
profile these are the torrents stranded by its missing session.

listen_port.description: The configured static listen port; `null` for a `natpmp` profile.

port_forward.description: How the listen port is chosen.

forwarded_port.description:
The effective listen port now: the NAT-PMP-negotiated port for a
`natpmp` profile, else the configured static port. `null` while a
`natpmp` profile has none, and for a `failed` profile.

user_agent.description:
The user agent the session announces with; `null` for a host profile
that did not override libtorrent's.

failure_reason.description: Why the profile has no session. Set only when `status` is `failed`.

Profile.description:
One profile: one libtorrent session, usually one tracker account behind
one VPN tunnel.

items.description:
Live profiles in the order their `[[profile]]` tables appear in the
config file, then the profiles that failed to come up, in config order
among themselves. The first entry is only `active` when at least one
profile came up: pick a default by filtering on `status`, not by
taking the first.

vpn_interface.description: The VPN interface the session binds to; `null` for a host profile.

allowed_tracker_domains.description:
Tracker domains this profile's torrents may announce to. Empty admits
any.

paused_for_vpn.description: Torrents currently paused because the tunnel went down.

port_forward_ok.description:
Whether the last NAT-PMP renewal succeeded. Always `true` for a
`static` profile, which has nothing to renew, and `false` for a
`failed` one.

ProfileDetail.description: One profile, with its tunnel and tracker configuration.

ProfileUnavailableReason.description: A profile's state, as far as a request needing it is concerned.

detail.description: The same, for a person: for a `failed` profile, its bring-up failure.

SkippedProfile.description: A profile a bulk operation did not act on.

torrent_count.description: Torrents the engine accepted the pause or resume for.

failed_count.description:
Torrents whose engine call failed. Nonzero means not everything was
reached.

skipped_profiles.description:
Profiles this request did not act on, each with why. Always empty for
a single profile's operation, which refuses instead.

BulkOutcome.description:
What a pause or resume of many torrents did.

A body rather than a bare `204`: a daemon-wide pause spans profiles that
can be in different states, and an operator stopping everything during an
incident has to see what was not reached.

bytes_adopted.description: Bytes claimed by a torrent that is adopted (loaded and seeding).

bytes_matched.description: Bytes claimed by a torrent that is matched but not yet adopted.

bytes_orphan.description: Bytes on disk that no torrent in the library claims.

files_orphan.description: Files no torrent in the library claims.

DirRollup.description:
Byte accounting for one directory subtree — what makes the pool legible at
petabyte scale, where a file listing is useless but "this subtree is 8 TB
and none of it is protected" is not.

root_id.description: The root's id, which every per-root operation takes.

path.description: The root's absolute path on the daemon's host.

missing.description: Torrents with no payload under any managed root.

partial.description: Torrents with some of their payload present.

matched.description: Torrents whose payload is complete and not yet adopted.

drifted.description: Torrents whose payload changed since it was last verified.

overlap.description: Torrents sharing a file with another torrent.

AdoptionCounts.description: How many library torrents are in each adoption state.

roots.description: Every managed root, with its byte accounting.

library_dir.description: The directory the library of `.torrent` files is read from.

states.description:
Library torrents by adoption state. A torrent never matched has no
state and is in none of these.

verify_queue_depth.description: Adopted torrents waiting for a verification slot.

verify_in_flight.description: Adopted torrents libtorrent is hashing now.

path.description:
The path relative to the root; pass it as `path` to list inside a
directory.

Whether this is a directory. Directories are inferred from indexed file
paths, so an empty directory never appears.

states.description:
Adoption states of the torrents claiming anything under this entry, so
a client can colour a row without a request per row. Always empty in
an orphan listing.

TreeEntry.description: One entry of a directory listing.

One page of a directory listing: directories first, then files, each

name.description: The torrent's name from its metainfo.

state.description:
Where it stands against the payload on disk; `null` until a scan has
matched it.

The directory, relative to its root, the payload was matched at;

profile_id.description:
The profile that owns it, as the library or an adoption recorded;
`null` when none has.

tags.description: The tags the previous client recorded.

has_fastresume.description:
Whether the previous client left resume data beside it, which lets an
adoption skip re-hashing.

PoolTorrent.description: A torrent in the pool's library.

items.description: This page's items, in the collection's order.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; `null` on the last one.

PoolTorrentPage.description: One page of library torrents, in infohash order.

partial.description: Torrents with some of their payload present.

missing.description: Torrents with none of their payload present.

overlap.description: Torrents sharing a file with another torrent.

errors.description:
Entries skipped because they could not be read; the daemon's log names
each, and `pool_scan_errors_total` counts them by kind.

drifted.description: Torrents now marked `drifted`: a claimed file changed or vanished.

files_changed.description: Claimed files whose size or modification time changed.

applied_at.description: When an apply last finished, successfully or not; `null` before.

PlanSummary.description: A plan without its steps, as a listing carries it.

items.description: This page's items, in the collection's order.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; `null` on the last one.

PlanPage.description: One page of plans, oldest first.

StepOp.description: One filesystem operation of a plan.

seq.description: The step's position; steps run in this order.

dst.description: Where a move puts it; `null` for a delete.

error.description: Why the step failed; `null` unless it did.

applied_at.description: When an apply last finished, successfully or not; `null` before.

Plan.description: A mutation plan: the exact diff an apply would make.

password.description: The operator password `[auth] password_hash` was made from.

CreateSession.description: The operator password, exchanged for a session token.

token.description:
The bearer token (`tds_…`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
It is shown once: the daemon keeps only its hash.

scopes.description: What the token may do: `read` and `write`, never `metrics`.

expires_at.description: When the token stops working, unless revoked sooner.

bytes_per_sec.description:
Bytes per second, at least 1. `null` (or absent) removes the limit;
the profile's and the daemon's limits still apply.

priority.description:
libtorrent's download priority: 0 skips the file, 1 is low, 4 normal,
7 top.

infohashes.description: Between 1 and 1000 torrents from the library.

path.description: The directory, relative to the root; empty for the whole root.

oneOf.description: Every library torrent whose payload was matched under a directory.

profile_id.description:
The profile whose session receives every adopted torrent. Always
required: a profile is an account identity, and there is no count of
profiles at which the daemon may pick one for the caller.

dry_run.description: Report what would happen and change nothing.

AdoptRequest.description: A request to adopt existing payload into a profile.

reason.description: Why it was not acted on, in prose for an operator.

RefusedTorrent.description: A torrent an adoption or verification did not act on, and why.

dry_run.description: Whether this was a dry run, which changed nothing.

fast_path.description:
Adopted in seed mode on the strength of the previous client's resume
data; these seed without re-hashing.

queued_for_verification.description:
Adopted without seed mode: libtorrent hashes each before it seeds, a
bounded number at a time.

refused.description: Not adopted, each with the reason.

verify_bytes.description:
Bytes libtorrent must read to verify the queued set — the number that
decides whether an adoption takes minutes or days.

AdoptionResult.description: What an adoption did, or would do.

requested.description: How many infohashes the request named.

skipped.description: Torrents not re-hashed, each with the reason.

infohash.description: The torrent; it must be `matched` or `adopted`.

dest_root_id.description: The managed root to move it to.

dest_rel.description: The destination directory, relative to that root.

oneOf.description: Move one torrent's payload to a new directory under a managed root.

prefix.description: The directory, relative to the root; empty for the whole root.

oneOf.description: Delete every file under a subtree that no torrent claims.

confirm_token.description:
The plan's `confirm_token`, for a plan that deletes data; `null` or
absent for any other.

failed.description: Steps that failed; an apply stops at the first.

skipped.description: Steps already done by an earlier apply, and not repeated.

status.description:
Where the plan stands now: `applied`, or `failed` when a step failed —
the plan's steps then show which, and why.

oneOf.description:
A magnet URI. The torrent has no name, size or file list until its
metadata arrives from peers.

A `.torrent` on the daemon's own filesystem, inside its `.torrent`
store, the pool's library, or a managed root.

data.description:
The `.torrent`'s bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded). At most
64 MiB decoded.

TorrentSource.description: Where a torrent's metadata comes from, tagged by `kind`.

profile_id.description:
The profile the torrent is assigned to, and so the account that
announces it. Required: there is no default profile to guess.

save_path.description:
Where to store the payload. Must lie inside `default_save_path` or a
managed root; `default_save_path` when absent.

source.description: Where the torrent's metadata comes from.

bearer.description: An opaque token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Static tokens (`tdp_…`) come from `torrentd new-token` and carry the scopes the config grants them; session tokens (`tds_…`) come from `POST /v1/sessions` and carry `read` and `write`. Scopes: `read` for every safe operation, `write` for every operation that changes state (it implies `read`), `metrics` for `GET /metrics` only.
